result.title: Claim Laundering: When Agent Decision Models Trust Records Over Reality
result.summary: Agent decision models select actions in a single forward pass from inputs that combine environmental observations with the agent's own record of previous actions. When an action fails silently, these sources can conflict: the record reports success, but the environment shows that the step did not take effect. We ask which source determines the next decision. Across Android screen traces, ALFWorld, and WebShop, we construct paired states that independently vary the observation, the logged action, and an explicit success claim. In all 12 configurations of four decision models and three domains, records have a larger average effect on commitment decisions than observations; after claimed-but-failed steps, the models still stop, advance, or purchase in 53-100% of cases. Yet the relevant evidence is often represented internally: linear probes on intermediate hidden states distinguish successful from failed steps on held-out apps, tasks, and goals (AUROC 0.77-1.00), and activation patching reveals increasing influence from records in later layers. We use this signal in EVIGATE, an intermediate-layer veto that requires no additional forward pass and adds 0.04-2.0% serving latency. Under injected silent failures, EVIGATE improves task success by 18.7 points in live ALFWorld agents, 5.0 in WebShop, and 5.1 in a phone simulator, and in WebShop and the simulator it also outperforms random vetoes at the same rate. Its effectiveness depends on representative calibration states: gates calibrated on offline counterfactual states do not transfer reliably to live agent trajectories.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察 agent 决策模型在环境观测与自身动作记录冲突（动作静默失败）时依据哪一来源决策：在 Android 界面、ALFWorld、WebShop 构建配对状态，发现记录对承诺决策的影响普遍大于观测；线性探针显示中间隐状态已可区分成功/失败步骤，激活补丁显示记录影响随层加深，并据此提出无需额外前向的中间层否决模块 EVIGATE。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及「答案是否使用 latent 内容／视觉旁路」与「LOOK 后是否 STOP」问题：其探针与激活补丁证据可供核查视觉证据虽被内部编码却未被决策采用的现象，EVIGATE 也是中间层干预的可借鉴线索。
